youtube.title: The most common septic install mistakes with an Eljen GSF

captions.instagram:
Yes, people still install these upside down.

Jimmy Bell and Zach Gardner of {eljen} see two mistakes on site over and over: fabric that isn't placed right, so it tents over the unit, and units going in upside down. It'll still work. It just works better right side up, which is why there's now a painted line and a logo on top.

Full episode on YouTube: {episode}

#septic #septicinstaller #drainfield #onsitewastewater
captions.facebook:
I asked the team at {eljen} what goes wrong most often when their system gets installed. Two things came up. The first is the fabric: if it isn't placed right, it tents up over the unit. The second is installers flipping the units upside down, often enough that Eljen added a spray-painted line and logos to show which side is up. Jimmy Bell and Zach Gardner say it'll still work upside down. It just works better right side up.

#septic

youtube.title: What can you plant on top of a septic drain field?

captions.instagram:
Thinking about carrots on the drain field? Skip them.

The question {eljen} hears most is what you can plant on top of the system. Shallow-root vegetables and wildflowers are fine. Right after that, people ask about driving over it, and the answer is no, unless it was engineered to take that load.

Full episode on YouTube: {episode}

#septic #drainfield #septictank #homeowner #gardening
captions.facebook:
If you've ever wondered what you can plant over a drain field, you're not alone. It's the question the team at {eljen} gets most, by phone and by email. Shallow-root vegetables and wildflowers are fine. Carrots aren't. The next thing people ask is whether they can drive over it, and the answer is no, unless the system was engineered to handle that weight.

#septic
